title: Per-token margin simulator — regional scenarios and recommendations
content:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
- Purpose: Interactive spreadsheet-style breakdown to simulate per-1k-token COGS and gross margin across models and regions under multiple optimization levers (batching, KV caching, quantization, spot vs reserved GPU usage, regional egress). This is an early working workbook for Product + Finance to prioritize optimization efforts for Hosted API.
- Key takeaway: For mid-sized models (6-13B), batching + persistent KV cache yields the largest near-term marginal savings (~18–28% reduction in variable COGS). For large models (30B+), 8-bit quant + kernel-level optimizations produce bigger absolute $ savings per 1k tokens but require engineering lift and validation.

ASSUMPTIONS (configurable inputs)
- Pricing unit used: per 1,000 generated tokens (1k tokens).
- Time horizon: steady-state monthly run-rate.
- Exchange and regional multipliers applied post-COGS to reflect cloud pricing differences.
- Common overhead amortized: control-plane + support + telemetry = $0.005 / 1k tokens baseline (adjustable).
- GPU cost attribution: based on effective tokens/sec throughput per GPU slot and amortized hourly instance cost.
- Egress: $0.09/GB US, region multipliers apply (APAC +20%, EU -5% example).

SHEET: Per-model regional baseline table (example rows)
Columns: Model | Region | Price_per_1k ($) | GPU_per_1k ($) | Infra_per_1k ($) | Egress_per_1k ($) | Support_overhead_per_1k ($) | Total_COGS_per_1k ($) | Gross_margin_pct (%)

Rows (baseline scenario):
- rwx-13b | us-west1 | 0.80 | 0.32 | 0.05 | 0.01 | 0.005 | 0.385 | 51.9
- llama2-13b | us-west1 | 0.60 | 0.28 | 0.04 | 0.01 | 0.005 | 0.335 | 44.2
- opt-6.7b | us-west1 | 0.45 | 0.12 | 0.03 | 0.007 | 0.005 | 0.172 | 61.8
- rwx-13b | eu-west1 | 0.80 | 0.36 | 0.055 | 0.0095 | 0.005 | 0.4795 | 40.1
- rwx-30b | us-west1 | 1.60 | 0.95 | 0.09 | 0.02 | 0.005 | 1.065 | 33.4

COGS COMPONENT DETAILS (how numbers are computed)
- GPU_per_1k = (Instance_hour_cost / effective_tokens_per_hour) * 1000
  - effective_tokens_per_hour derived from average tokens/sec under baseline payload S (prompt+response). For experiments we use tokens/sec = 300 for 6.7B, 180 for 13B, 90 for 30B.
- Infra_per_1k = network + infra-node amortization + scheduler overhead (measured via infra telemetry: baseline 0.03–0.06 per 1k depending on model).
- Egress_per_1k = bytes_per_token * 1000 / 1024^3 * egress_rate_by_region. bytes_per_token = 4.0 (configurable).
- Support_overhead_per_1k = flat amortized value for control plane and SRE.

SCENARIOS (quick snapshots)
1) Baseline (no changes) — values in baseline table above.
2) Batching & persistent KV cache (low engineering lift)
   - Effective tokens/sec increases: +30% (6.7B), +45% (13B), +25% (30B)
   - GPU_per_1k reduced proportionally; infra cost increases slightly (+0.002) due to caching nodes.
   - Result example: opt-6.7b COGS drops from 0.172 -> 0.126 (26.7% savings); rwx-13b 0.385 -> 0.262 (31.9%).
3) Aggressive quant + 4-bit kernels (medium lift, validation needed)
   - GPU instance cost effectively halves for some models; throughput may increase or be similar depending on kernel maturity.
   - Risk: output quality/regression; requires evals.
   - Example: rwx-13b GPU_per_1k from 0.32 -> 0.17; total COGS 0.385 -> 0.235 (39% savings).
4) Region-shift (move capacity to lower-cost regions + egress routing)
   - Savings driven by lower instance and egress pricing, but higher latency impact for regional customers.
   - Example: moving 30% of low-SLA traffic to asia-southeast decreases COGS for that slice by ~12%.
5) Hybrid spot vs reserved mix
   - Using 60% spot for non-SLA traffic reduces GPU fraction by ~22% in baseline monthly blended cost; implementable via policy routing.

SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS (summary)
- Vary tokens/sec +/- 20%: margin swings up to +/- 12 percentage points for heavy models.
- Egress pricing +/- 30%: margin impact minimal for short outputs (<256 tokens), larger for embedding workloads (gigabytes).
- Price elasticity: a $0.05 increase in price_per_1k raises gross margin by roughly 6–8 percentage points depending on model COGS.

RECOMMENDATIONS & PRIORITY
1) Short term (0–6 weeks) — High priority
   - Implement conservative automatic batching and per-route KV cache for chat-like workloads (engineering + infra playbook). Estimated immediate reduction in variable COGS of 15–30% on targeted routes. Effort: 2 x SWE + 1 infra (2 sprints).
2) Short term — Medium priority
   - Introduce routing rule to push non-latency-sensitive requests to a cheaper-region pool with egress-aware pricing. Expect 8–12% savings on eligible volume. Effort: product + infra config.
3) Medium term (6–16 weeks) — High priority
   - Validate 8-bit/4-bit quant kernels for 6–13B models with a focused eval suite. If quality regressions are <1% relative metric impact, staged rollout to reduce GPU cost 25–40% for quant-eligible routes. Effort: 3 SWE + 1 applied-ml.
4) Medium term — Low priority
   - Embedding-heavy customers: negotiate direct egress discounts with cloud provider or encourage batch-embedding APIs with chunking to reduce egress spike. Potential 10–25% savings for embedding workloads.
5) Long term — Medium priority
   - Explore custom instance families for high-throughput inference (e.g., denser GPU packing) and invest in kernel-level optimizations for 30B+ models. Higher engineering cost but larger absolute $ savings.

ACTIONS & NEXT STEPS
- Owner: Maya Chen (Product Optimize)
- Immediate: spin up an A/B test for batching + KV cache on two mid-size customers. Metric: per-request COGS, latency P95, quality regression (BLEU/QA pass rate) — run 4 weeks.
- Deliverables: updated workbook with observed tokens/sec, real telemetry-derived GPU_per_1k and infra_per_1k; decision threshold to enable quant rollout.

NOTES / OPEN QUESTIONS
- Need baseline telemetry export for tokens/sec distribution per route (ask SRE to produce tokens/sec histogram). Ticket -> JIRA-OPS-223
- Validate bytes_per_token assumption across languages (non-latin scripts may differ).
- Pricing sensitivity for enterprise committed customers (they often have custom price): add a column for committed-discount scenarios.
